name: jobs/retry-safety
summary: Make background jobs safe under duplicate delivery, retries, and partial failure.
intent: A background job can be delivered more than once or retried after interruption without duplicating protected side effects, while transient failures still retry and permanent failures remain observable.

rules.text: Each logical job has a stable identity or idempotency key that survives retries of the same work.
A duplicate delivery cannot repeat a protected side effect that has already completed successfully.
Transient failures use the host queue's retry mechanism with an explicit retry or backoff policy.
A job that exhausts retries remains observable through the host system's failed-job, dead-letter, or equivalent mechanism.

invariants.text: The implementation uses the repository's existing queue ownership and worker lifecycle instead of adding a parallel scheduler without need.
Failures are not swallowed merely to make the queue consider the job successful.
Jobs not opted into this behavior keep their existing retry semantics.

security.text: Idempotency state and protected side effects cannot diverge in a way that permits a completed effect to execute again after a crash.
A reused logical job identity cannot silently authorize materially different work without an explicit conflict or versioning rule.

acceptance.text: Delivering the same logical job twice executes the protected side effect once.
A transient failure is retried according to the configured policy and can subsequently complete.
A simulated interruption around the protected side effect does not produce a duplicate completed effect after retry.
A permanently failing job reaches the host system's observable terminal-failure path after the configured attempts.
